question: Which of the following drugs used in the treatment of female infertility is an analogue of the gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) capable of inhibiting gonadal steroidogenesis during continued treatment ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Buserelin -> GnRH analogue -> inhibits gonadal steroidogenesis -> 95% CHAIN: Cetrorelix -> GnRH analogue -> inhibits gonadal steroidogenesis -> 95%
enhanced_information: Buserelin and Cetrorelix are GnRH analogues capable of inhibiting gonadal steroidogenesis during continued treatment. This is supported by the fact that both drugs act on the GnRH pathway, leading to the suppression of gonadal steroid hormone production. Evidence paths show interactions between GnRH and steroid hormones in gonadal structures, reinforcing the mechanism of action of these drugs.
analysis: Buserelin and Cetrorelix are GnRH analogues capable of inhibiting gonadal steroidogenesis during continued treatment. This aligns with the known mechanism of action of GnRH analogues in suppressing gonadal steroid hormone production. Progesterone is not an analogue of GnRH and does not inhibit gonadal steroidogenesis. Clomiphene, although used in female infertility, does not act as a GnRH analogue capable of inhibiting gonadal steroidogenesis. Therefore, the most likely correct option is Cetrorelix.
